Do **not** automatically refresh marts or modify data. --- ### Investigation steps | Issue | Primary runbook | Key actions | |-------|----------------|-------------| | **Mart‑parity mismatch** | `[runbook:reconciliation:1:0]` | • Run `warehouse_mart_parity` to compare fact candle totals & quote volume against the hourly activity mart.
• Note the observed time and batch status; mismatches can stem from refresh timing, scope differences, or a load defect.
• If the mismatch persists, move to reconciliation checks. | | **Reconciliation mismatch** | `[runbook:reconciliation:0:0]` | • Execute `warehouse_reconciliation` and confirm `staging_rows = rejected_rows + duplicate_rows + accepted_rows`.
• Any non‑zero `accounting_delta` signals a problem – examine the specific batch and its load report.

• Run `warehouse_lineage` to trace facts back to archive hashes and source files.
• If no quality checks are returned, treat it as “no evidence of perfect data,” not proof of health.
• Escalate to a scoped operator investigation; avoid automatic mart refreshes or data edits. | --- ### Quick reference flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Detect mismatch] --> B{Mart parity?} B -- Yes --> C[Run warehouse_mart_parity] --> D[Check batch timing & scope] B -- No --> E[Run warehouse_reconciliation] --> F[Inspect accounting_delta] D --> G[If still mismatched → run reconciliation steps] F --> G G --> H[Run warehouse_quality & warehouse_lineage] H --> I[Operator scoped investigation] ``` --- **What you need to run** - `warehouse_mart_parity` – to see the exact totals that differ. - `warehouse_reconciliation` – to verify accounting balance. - `warehouse_quality` – to locate failed validation checks. - `warehouse_lineage` – to trace the origin of the offending rows.
